referenceRoles: Open-source screenshots are visual inspiration; CareerAtlas images are continuity references or explicit edit targets.
editor:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create realistic, production-quality desktop web app UI for CareerAtlas, a career evidence knowledge system. This is one screen in a coordinated suite, NOT alternative competing styles. Target dimensions 1440 x 1024. Current date 2026-11-17, use no future timestamps. English UI labels and fictional demo data; initial product locale undecided.
Attached images are visual inspiration only: shadcn-vue component styling, shadcn dashboard shell, and Shadcn Admin compact navigation. Borrow clean typography, restrained sidebar, thin dividers, sober whitespace, small 8px radii, subtle gray surfaces. Do NOT copy analytics, finance widgets, branding or charts. Vue 3 + shadcn-vue design. White main background #FFFFFF, pale gray sidebar #F8FAFC, dark ink #17221F, muted text #52615A, dark emerald primary #047857, mint selected surface #ECFDF5, amber pending #92400E. Inter/system sans type, 14-16px body, 30px page heading. Crisp readable text, spacious intentional alignment, not a whole app floating in a card; no nested cards, no decorative gradients or illustrations, no skill scores or invented metrics. Actual app content only, no browser frame, no device bezel. Simple library-style outline icons. One clear primary action per screen. Footer unobtrusively "Fictional demo data". P0 only; no AI capture, interview, organizations or opportunity menu. Owner UI sidebar width 216 with wordmark CareerAtlas, small "Personal workspace", navigation "Projects", "Skills", "Profile", "Publish", bottom demo user "Alex Morgan". Explicit provenance: supplied URLs not independently verified; owner confirmation not reviewer certification.
Screen name: Evidence-first editor. Sidebar Projects active. Slim top breadcrumb "Projects / Atlas Notes / Experience". Heading "Capture your contribution" and subtitle "Keep the work, your actions and the evidence connected." Status "Draft · Private".
Two columns: main editor about 720 wide, right evidence rail about 300 wide. Main form has title "Accessible project search", project "Atlas Notes" and type "Personal project", role "Frontend developer". Date field "October 2026" with precision selector "Month". Keep required labels asterisk on title, project, type, date, personal action. Section "My contribution" text area "I built the search interface, added keyboard navigation and wrote component tests." Distinct section "Team outcome (optional)" text "The team released the project search workflow." Optional background can be collapsed. Small note "A measurable result is optional." Skills chips Vue 3, TypeScript, Accessibility with Add skill. Right rail heading "Supporting evidence", two compact rows "Pull request #24 · Supplied link" and "Keyboard test notes · Owner statement", subdued note "Links have not been independently verified." Add evidence button. Lower right rail pale neutral note "Confirmation keeps this record private. Publishing is a separate step." Bottom fixed action area aligns right secondary "Save draft" and one emerald primary "Confirm experience". At the very bottom textual saved indicator "Draft saved · 17 Nov 2026". No publication buttons on this screen. Dense enough to be useful, generous whitespace, every label clearly readable.
editorRevision: Edit the attached CareerAtlas experience editor. Preserve every part of layout and design except two exact text replacements in the upper form: change the label 'Type *' to 'Record type *'; change its dropdown value 'Personal project' to 'Work contribution'. This field describes the experience record, not the project's type. Keep 'Atlas Notes' as project, all other fields, text, dates, colors, buttons, and dimensions exactly unchanged.

Below columns a calm publication statement "Publishing creates a snapshot. Later edits stay private until you publish again." publicationRevision: Edit the attached CareerAtlas publication preview UI. Preserve every pixel of layout, colors, typography, all wording and controls except this one precise change: in the left Public content checklist, change the checkbox directly before 'Team outcome' from a green checked checkbox to an empty unchecked white checkbox with gray outline, just like Contact links. Do not change any other checkbox. The right preview correctly omits Team outcome, so this edit makes the selection match the preview. Keep image dimensions and all other content unchanged.

Screen name: Public evidence portfolio. Match the attached CareerAtlas screen's typography, white/emerald colors, fine dividers and sober visual language. Visitor-facing surface, NO owner sidebar, editing controls or private metadata. Full-width slim header with CareerAtlas left, "Projects", "Skills" nav right. Spacious max-width 1200px reading container. Small "PUBLIC PORTFOLIO" overline, large "Alex Morgan" heading, "Frontend developer" and bio "I build accessible interfaces and document how they work." Under it "Published 17 Nov 2026". Hero not excessively tall.
Below hero split 60/40. Left project editorial layout, right Q&A panel. Left heading "Selected work" then "Atlas Notes", metadata "Personal project · October 2026", short overview "A searchable workspace for project notes.", distinct "My contribution" paragraph "Built the search interface, keyboard navigation and component tests.", skills chips Vue 3, TypeScript, Accessibility. A discreet text action "Read project". Section "Evidence" with row "Pull request #24 · Supplied link" and note "Not independently verified." No team outcome because omitted in this publication, no contact because excluded.
Right panel heading "Ask about this work", subline "Answers use this published portfolio only." A subtle user question bubble "What did Alex build in Vue?" Clear unboxed assistant response "Alex built the search interface and keyboard navigation for Atlas Notes, and wrote component tests. [1]" Followed one clickable citation source row with visible "[1] Atlas Notes", "Accessible project search", "Published 17 Nov 2026". Citation visual emphasis is clear and accessible. Another suggested question text button "What evidence supports this?" Bottom input with placeholder "Ask about a project or skill..." and emerald send button. Small text "AI-generated answers may need checking. Inspect the sources." Bottom of whole page "Fictional demo data". No reviewer certification badge, no hiring or skill scores, no general-purpose chatbot features, no file uploads or model selectors. Generous negative space, concise content, clean mature product design.
